src/client/Main.luau.header:
Port of scripts/main.gd: the client root. Creates the AudioDirector, the globe (WorldView) and the
interface (UIRoot), wires them to the Session, and owns the top-bar buttons that the original put in
Airship's HUD bar: Music toggle (also key M), Help, Leaderboard, Home → focus your nation (also key
Home) and the Game menu. The buttons sit in Roblox's own top-bar row, right of Roblox's menu / chat
buttons (GuiService.TopbarInset), styled like them. Match-only buttons hide on the title screen.

UIRoot must NOT bind M / Home or call world:bind_state itself (DESIGN.md §10).
Missing modules (during development) are skipped so boot never errors.

src/client/Session.luau.header:
Port of scripts/net/session.gd (client half): match orchestration for the title attract mode, solo
campaigns and the shared multiplayer match. Same public API and signals as session.gd.

  MODE_TITLE  local AI-only Sim (88 nations + tribes): a fast warm-up time-lapse, then TITLE_SPEED
  MODE_SOLO   local Sim with one human, paused while help / game menu are open
  MODE_MULTI  the server's Sim (src/server/MatchServer.luau): snapshot then per-tick deltas

session.gd built and stepped local sims on a worker thread. Roblox gives game scripts no worker
threads, so here:
  * match construction (Sim.new, add_human, snapshot, GameState load) and multiplayer snapshot
    decoding run in a Coop job (Net/Coop.luau) resumed every frame with BUILD_BUDGET_S — the previous
    world keeps animating meanwhile, and nothing blocks a frame as long as the Core loops call
    Coop.check();
  * local stepping is budgeted: a tick's step is itself a Coop job (the Sim's loops call
    Coop.check()), resumed every frame with STEP_BUDGET_S until it completes, then further ticks
    while the budget lasts. A time-lapse that can't keep up slows down instead of stalling frames
    (the accumulator is capped exactly like session.gd's MAX_STEPS_PER_TASK).

The environment is injectable (`Session.new(env)`) so tests drive the multiplayer path headless
against MatchServer (tests/net_session.luau). On Roblox `Session.new()` builds the real environment.

Maps: local matches run on config.map_id (start_solo's optional map id; the title uses the default
map); a multiplayer mirror uses the snapshot's map_id. A map that is not available locally (only
the default map is replicated) is downloaded first (env.fetch_map_async → Net/MapFetch) while the
build / join job waits; the lobby info's map_id is prefetched.

src/client/Dev/AssetsAudio.luau.header:
Assets agent dev harness: verifies every Audio manifest entry loads and plays (AF_DEV = "AssetsAudio").
Silent: Sounds play at Volume 0; loudness is measured with AudioPlayer -> AudioAnalyzer (not wired

  fetch    ContentProvider:PreloadAsync status
  loaded   Sound.IsLoaded, TimeLength vs manifest length
  plays    TimePosition advances after :Play()
  loop     music only: Looped sound started 0.4 s before the end wraps to ~0.4 s (DidLoop fired)
  peak     max AudioAnalyzer.PeakLevel while playing (compare with the source WAV's sample peak)

src/client/Dev/AssetsIcons.luau.header:
Assets agent dev harness: contact sheet of every UiIcons / Branding image (AF_DEV = "AssetsIcons").

Also reads every uploaded image back (EditableImage) and prints per-image channel sums as JSON so
the generator's PNGs can be compared byte-for-byte ("[AssetsIcons] readback {...}").

src/client/Dev/Film.luau.header:
Studio only (Dev: not published). Films the game a frame at a time for the trailer (2026-10-12: the
trailer for the experience's details page): while it runs,
time stands still (Map/FrameClock: dt 0) until the capture script asks for the next frame, which
moves time on by exactly 1/FPS s. The session, the map, its animations and the HUD's own tweens all
run on that time, so frames captured one by one (Studio MCP screen_capture, slow) play back smooth
at FPS. Roblox's TweenService still runs on real time.

The capture script sets workspace attribute af_film_req = n (n counting up) and waits for
af_film_done = n: that frame has been drawn (signalled a frame later), and stays on screen.

  Film.start(Main, fps?)   Film.stop()
The camera is moved with `film cam` / `film look` (Dev/SessionDiag): its glides run on its own dt,
so on film time.

src/client/UI/Arsenal.luau.header:
The Arsenal (2026-10-04: units like Artillery and special nukes, unlocked by grinding Stars or
with Robux): a modal for the items of Data/Arsenal. It opens from the
title (ArsenalButton), from the command bar's SHOP button, and on its item when a locked unit is
pressed in a match.

One item at a time (2026-10-24: the old menu was so confusing that players opened it and bought
nothing; of 4.63M opens in a week,
164K pressed a price). It was a grid of eight cards, each with an unlabeled Stars pill and an
unlabeled Robux pill under a small busy scene.
  list     on the left, the items grouped NUKES / ARMY / BOOSTS: each a row with its render, its name
           and what it takes: OWNED, its Stars when the player has enough, else its Robux price. A
           press shows it on the right.
  item     on the right: what it does in a match, playing big (UI/ArsenalDemo); its name, what kind
           of thing it is and FOREVER; one plain sentence (Data/Arsenal `plain`) and two facts. Then
           one big BUY NOW button with the Robux price, and under it the other way: OR UNLOCK WITH
           ★ 20,000 when the player has the Stars (a press asks once more, the second spends them),
           else how far along they are with a bar. An item the player has reads OWNED.
  header   the title, one line of what this is, the Stars balance, close.
It opens on the item it was asked for, else the first one the player's Stars can unlock, else the
first one they don't have. An unlock (Session.unlocked, however it was bought) flashes its item.
It closes from its close button or a press outside the window, never from a press on the window.
Signals: closed.

src/client/UI/ArsenalButton.luau.header:

src/client/UI/ArsenalDemo.luau.header:
The Arsenal's gameplay previews: each card's art plays a few seconds of what its item does in a
match, over and over (2026-10-12: the shop shows gameplay, as too few players were using it).
The scene is drawn like the
map: the player's land on the left, a nation's on the right with a city, its name and its troops,
the structures' plates (Assets/MapSprites, Assets/ArsenalArt). The ground is a piece of a real map
drawn the way a match draws it (Assets/ArsenalMaps: terrain, rivers and coasts, the territories
blended over them with their borders, a pixel a tile; 2026-10-24: a real map in place of
the solid background colours, which looked bad). Flat colours stand in without it.

What flies and what blows up is drawn art (the same day: real graphics in place of the pixel
circles, so that nukes and the other items look better): the shop
cards' own renders for the missiles and the bomber (Assets/ArsenalArt.renders), and effects drawn by
tools/assets/make_arsenal_fx.py (Assets/ArsenalFx): a fireball flipbook, a mushroom cloud, smoke
trails, shockwaves, scorch marks, a beam, tracers, bombs, warheads, a reticle, parachutes. Big hits
shake the scene.
  mega       the missile arcs from the silo onto the city under a reticle: a white flash, a
             shockwave, a mushroom cloud, the city gone, fallout
  scatter    the missile splits over the city into five warheads, five fireballs
  reinforce  three paratroopers drop in (+2.0K each), then the border advances into the nation
  artillery  the battery fires a tracer every second or so into its range ring
  airfield   a bomber takes off, crosses a marked spot and drops three bombs on it
  railgun    it charges, then a beam crosses the whole scene: no range limit
  stars2x    a payout, and a "2X" stamp doubling it
  reload2x   two silos, the rapid one firing twice for the other's once
Everything is a function of the time into the loop (no state carried between frames), so a demo
starts anywhere and always shows a whole loop.

  ArsenalDemo.new(parent, item, size_px, u, phase) -> demo;  demo:step(now);  demo:destroy()
  ArsenalDemo.preload()  fetches the art once (the Arsenal calls it when it opens)

src/client/UI/CommandBar.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/command_bar.gd (UICommandBar)
Bottom command bar: nation chip, troops (with cap, growth and fill), the attack-ratio slider, gold
(with income, next to the slots it buys) and the ten build / nuke slots. Re-flows between a single
row (wide desktop), two rows (laptop / tablet) and a slim phone strip (icons + numbers, a short
slider and a Build toggle; the slots live in a tray and the details in a tap-for-info card).

The Arsenal (Data/Arsenal; 2026-10-04): one gold SHOP slot closes the row and opens the
Arsenal; a kind the player has unlocked gets a slot of its own before it, a locked one has none
(2026-10-04: the build menu was too big, so only the SHOP button shows and it all stays on one
row; the first version had a second row of eight locked slots). The SHOP slot is one gold button
that shows, in turn, what the player has yet to get (ShopSlot; 2026-10-12: one button instead of
six sub-buttons, the locked units' cards it held from 2026-10-05). On phones the slots
narrow a little, then the SHOP button, before the tray takes a second row (TrayFit).

Signals: build_chosen(kind), cancel_placement(), footprint_changed(), stats_tapped(),
arsenal_wanted(key?, from?) (the SHOP button; key: the item it showed).
Members read by UIRoot / UIInteract: panel, tray, buttons, _place_chip, _slider, _tray_btn, _flow.
Per frame: update(dt) (GDScript _process).

src/client/UI/CrateButton.luau.header:
The title screen's crate button, top right (2026-09-29: on phones the chest button was hard to
notice, so it got more to catch the eye). The 3D chest (ChestView) wiggles on a glow and slow
rays with a twinkle or two, a CRATES pill under it, and a badge:
  a crate waiting (bought, not opened)  a red count, the pill says OPEN, it wiggles more often;
  the first crate not bought yet        its price (15) with the Robux icon;
  otherwise                             no badge.

src/client/UI/CrateOpening.luau.header:
Opening a cosmetic crate: a Clash Royale-style show around a 3D chest (2026-09-29: the first version
of opening a crate was not satisfying at all, and it should be super fun; the show was then made
3D, around a ready-made voxel chest).
The chest is BedWars' voxel block chest (Assets/CrateModel) in a
ViewportFrame; the choreography follows Tribes' drop reveal (the same studio's game).
  land    the screen dims; the chest falls in stretched past air streaks, lands with a squash, dust,
          a floor ring and a shake; the title slams in;
  idle    it bobs; every WIGGLE_EVERY_S it wiggles with a rattle, the lid cracks and light leaks out;
          "TAP TO OPEN". It never opens by itself (no auto-open: the player has to click or tap
          it open);
  build   tapped: distinct rattles, closer together and bigger, while the light turns the item's
          rarity colour and BedWars' lucky box preview for that rarity plays; the rarer the item, the
          longer the build (BUILD_S; Epic and Legendary tease with rays); a roll still on its way
          keeps it rattling (the network wait hides in there);
  burst   a crouch, then the lid bursts open: a flash in the rarity colour, rays, a light beam and
          sparks out of the chest, a shockwave ring, a shake;
  card    the card flies out of the chest face down while the chest steps down; it glows in its
          rarity colour (CARD_HOLD_S: longer for the rarer ones, a tap hurries it), then flips: the
          item, NEW!, the rarity, the name, the rarity's sound;
  choose  WEAR IT · OPEN ANOTHER (a waiting crate, or the next one's price) · DONE.
Nothing clips to white: flashes are the rarity colour at part strength.
Locker drives it: play(info) as the crate is opened, resolve(item_id) / fail(text) from the server.
Signals: wear(item_id), again(), closed(fail_text?), shown(open). `pace` > 1 slows the whole show
(frame captures).

src/client/UI/GlassPanel.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/glass_panel.gd (UIGlass)
Frosted-glass panel: navy tint, 1 px light border, a top sheen line and a soft drop shadow.
Lays out its children like a PanelContainer (inside the padding).

Roblox has no backdrop blur, so the glass is drawn as the GDScript no-frost path does (a flat
translucent tint, UITheme.GLASS_BOOST more opaque) plus the frost shader's top sheen gradient.
Parts: shadow (9-slice, Assets/UIKit shadows) < tint (UICorner + inner UIStroke border)
< sheen gradient < sheen line / accent stripe < content.

src/client/UI/GlobeNotice.luau.header:
Territory-map notice (review_code.md R2-3). The globe draws territory colours with Editable
images / meshes; when the device's editable budget is exhausted, or the experience's Mesh / Image
APIs permission is off in a published place, it falls back to the static globe (WorldView
territory_status().state == "unavailable"). Instead of a silent console warning the player gets
this small card: non-blocking (the game keeps running underneath), styled like the Coach tip
card, dismissible, hidden again by itself when territories come back. The place owner (Studio, or
the account / group that owns the experience) also sees how to enable the APIs.

API: GlobeNotice.new(ctx), set_status(status), apply_layout(blockers: { Rect }), card (GlassPanel).

src/client/UI/HelpOverlay.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/help_overlay.gd (UIHelpOverlay)
"How to play" overlay: illustrated sections (spawn, expand & attack, boats, economy, nukes,
alliances, victory) and the mouse/keyboard and touch controls. Scrolls on small screens.

Also defines two small containers the kit does not ship: Scroll (ScrollContainer, vertical)
and Grid (GridContainer), both with Godot layout semantics.

src/client/UI/HoldRing.luau.header:
Touch: a ring that closes in around a finger held on the map until the long-press menu opens
(2026-09-29: the press-and-hold quick build menu felt inconsistent on phones). It shows that the
hold is counting (keep still) and when it will open. Driven each frame by UIRoot from
MapInput.hold_state(); drawn on a raw logical-px canvas (UICtx.canvas), input-transparent.

src/client/UI/Leaderboard.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/leaderboard.gd (UILeaderboard)
Right-side leaderboard: top 10 by land share with colour, name, land % and troops. Your own row
is pinned when you are outside the top 10; allies and traitors are marked. Clicking a row focuses
the camera on that nation. On phones it collapses into a rank pill. Game admins see a person icon on
real players' rows, and every real player outside the top is pinned below it (one click away).

Every match starts with the board closed (close_for_match): the pill (the status pill on phones)
opens it, and it stays as the player leaves it until the match ends (since 2026-10-09).
Until then a desktop started open and remembered the player's
last choice in the saved settings (leaderboard_open_desktop / _touch: old records keep the keys,
nothing reads them); a report of the same week: the logs on the left-hand side blocked parts of the
map.

Signals: toggled(open). Members: panel, _pill, expanded, user_hidden, pill_enabled.
Methods: set_open(on), toggle(), close_for_match(), apply_layout(top), place_pill_left_of(rect),
bottom_edge(), my_rank(), mark_dirty(), refresh(); per frame update(dt).

src/client/UI/Locker.luau.header:
The Locker (2026-09-29: cosmetic loot boxes of territory skins and flags to unlock):
a modal from the title with the crate card on the left and what you own on the right.
  crate card  the crate art, "a territory skin or a flag you don't own yet", the player's own odds
              per rarity (Cosmetics.odds, shown before every purchase: Roblox's paid random items
              rules), how many items they own, and the button: 15 Robux for the first crate, 49
              after (Data/Products), "Open" while a bought crate waits; under it three crates for
              less (Data/Products crate3, _pack_saving). Hidden where paid random
              items are restricted (Session.inventory.crates_allowed, PolicyService on the server).
  grid        Skins / Flags tabs: every item (owned bright, the rest dimmed as a preview of what a
              crate can give); press an owned one to wear it, "None" to wear nothing. An exclusive
              skin (Cosmetics.exclusives) shows only to its owner, first, "EXCLUSIVE" in pink.
  reveal      after a crate opens: the item in its rarity's colour, Equip / Open another / Done.
The purchase goes like the takeover's (Takeover.luau): Roblox's prompt, the server stores the crate
(server/Purchases), the client opens it (Session.open_crate), the server rolls it.
Signals: closed.

src/client/UI/MapPicker.luau.header:
Map picker (the single-player map list): a modal grid of map cards (thumbnail, name, size) under
category tabs. The footer names the public-domain data the World map is made from. The grid is a Roblox
ScrollingFrame with a UIGridLayout hosted in a kit Control (the kit has no scroll container); card
sizes follow UITheme.scale.
Signals: picked(map_id), closed.
Entries come from set_entries({ {id, name, width, height, categories, thumb}, ... }).

src/client/UI/PartyPanel.luau.header:
The party on the title screen (server/Party; team games on: Rofront Staging only for now). Who is
in it (the leader picks the public match and everyone goes with them; a team game puts them on one
team), the invites to answer, and an invite list: the players on this server, and a Roblox invite

  PartyPanel.new(ctx) · set_state(state) · apply_layout() · on_action = function(action, user_id?)
Phones: a PARTY button that opens and closes the panel.

src/client/UI/PauseMenu.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/pause_menu.gd (UIPauseMenu)
Game menu: resume, how to play, settings, and leave / surrender with a confirmation step.

The same window has a second page, SETTINGS (2026-10-07, with a new switch to turn off the
pop expansion sound): the music, border pop, territory label and
"select before attacking" switches and "Show tips again", which stood in the game menu itself

src/client/UI/PlaceConfirm.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/place_confirm.gd (UIPlaceConfirm)
Touch placement / launch confirmation: a small caption and two big buttons (✕ cancel, ✓ build
or launch) floating next to the ghost on the globe, never over it. The buttons follow the
ghost's screen position every frame; UIInteract moves the ghost (tap elsewhere, map drag).

src/client/UI/Prices.luau.header:
The Robux prices the interface shows: Roblox's own for this player (MarketplaceService), never
the number in Data/Products once Roblox has answered. With Managed Pricing (dynamic pricing,
on since 2026-10-05) a product's price differs by region and while Roblox tests prices, and a

  Prices.robux(key)  the price of Data/Products[key]: Roblox's, or the set one until it answers
  Prices.fetch()     ask Roblox for every product's price (at most once every REFRESH_S), but the

src/client/UI/RadialMenu.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/radial_menu.gd
Circular context menu (right-click / long-press). Segments carry an icon and a short label;
unavailable actions are greyed and explain themselves in the caption under the ring. Items with
a `sub` list open a second ring (Build ▸, Nuke ▸); the centre button goes back / closes.

Roblox: drawn with plain instances in a logical-px canvas. Ring segments are static annular
sector masks (Assets/UiShapes, tools/ui/make_shapes.py) rotated into place and tinted; circles
are Frames with UICorner / UIStroke. While open, a full-screen button swallows pointer input
(Godot MOUSE_FILTER_STOP) and the opening finger of a long-press is followed through
UserInputService (press-slide-release picks).

src/client/UI/RatioSlider.luau.header:
The Attack bar: the share of the army an order sends, bound to UICtx.ratio. Five stops in one row
(UICtx.RATIO_STOPS: 10% 25% 35% 50% 75%), each one a labelled target: tap a stop, or drag across
them, and the amber thumb moves to it. The mouse wheel steps one stop.

It was a slider (a port of scripts/ui/ratio_slider.gd): 1% to 100% in steps of 1%, on a phone a
knob on a 96 px track, replaced 2026-10-08: it was too small and hard to drag to the right spot,
and a few fixed stops are simpler, at better breakpoints (10%, 25%, 35%,
50%, 75%). The tutorial's step on it lost 19.4% of the players who reached it (Tutorial funnel,
2026-10-07): what it asked for, 27% to 45%, was 17 px of that track.

A stop above UICtx.ratio_max (the tutorial stops at 50%) is drawn faint, and a tap on it sets the
highest stop allowed.

src/client/UI/RotateCard.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/rotate_card.gd (UIRotateCard)
Full-screen "Rotate your phone" card shown on touch devices while the viewport is portrait
(the game is designed for landscape; StarterGui.ScreenOrientation normally keeps us there).

src/client/UI/ShopButton.luau.header:
The title screen's flag shop button (Data/Shop; 2026-10-22: a daily rotating shop of flags for
sale), under the Arsenal and crate buttons: a purple card with the shop's flags taking
turns on its left, FLAG SHOP, the running set's name (HALLOWEEN FLAGS) or NEW FLAGS DAILY, and the
clock to the next shop. A NEW sticker until the player has opened today's shop (setting
"shop_seen_day"). pressed() -> UIRoot opens the shop (FlagShop). Shown while the shop has something
on sale here (FlagShop.on_sale).

src/client/UI/ShopLayout.luau.header:
The flag shop's layout (UI/FlagShop), apart so tests can run it without Roblox: the order of a
section's cards and where each goes, with a section's Legendary on a FEATURED card 2 x 2 cells big
(2026-10-24).

src/client/UI/ShopSlot.luau.header:
The SHOP button that closes the build row (CommandBar): one gold button, a little wider than a build
slot, that opens the Arsenal (2026-10-12: one button instead of six sub-buttons, as too few players
were opening the shop and more of them should click it; from 2026-10-05
it held a small card for each locked unit, before that it was a plain glass slot).

Solid gold with SHOP on it in dark letters. Over the word, the render of something the player has
yet to get (Assets/ArsenalArt.renders, the shop cards' pictures), a new one every CYCLE_S; a shine
crosses it every SHINE_S. Until the player has opened the Arsenal in this session, a red badge
counts what there is to get and the button gives a little shake every WIGGLE_S. With everything
got it is the Arsenal's shield over SHOP, still gold.

A press opens the Arsenal on the item it shows.

Signals: wanted(key: string?, from: string) (from: "match", for the analytics).

src/client/UI/SpawnOverlay.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/spawn_overlay.gd (UISpawnOverlay)
Spawn-phase banner: "Choose your starting location", a countdown ring, the solo "Deploying in 5…"
count and, in multiplayer, how many commanders have placed their capitals.

One slim row: two lines of text, the count (on a wide screen with a few of the commanders' head
shots before it) and the ring. It was a tall panel once: an icon disc, a line of advice and a
chip per commander, up to twelve of them over five rows: too big, so it was redesigned smaller
(2026-10-05).

src/client/UI/StarterButton.luau.header:
The title screen's starter pack button, under the Arsenal and crate buttons, while the starter pack's
offer runs (Data/Starter; 2026-10-15: available for a limited time only): a red card with the
Mega Nuke's render, STARTER PACK, the regular price struck through
beside the offer's, ENDS IN and the clock, a red "-76%" sticker on its corner and a light that
crosses it every few seconds. pressed() -> UIRoot opens the offer (StarterOffer). Hidden when there
is no running offer.

src/client/UI/StarterOffer.luau.header:
The starter pack's offer (Data/Starter; 2026-10-15: the starter pack at 39 Robux, on sale for a
limited time only). A window over the title: LIMITED-TIME OFFER,
STARTER PACK, the three items it unlocks (their shop renders on a glow of their colour, name and one
line), the regular price struck through beside the offer's with a red "-76%" sticker (both Roblox's
live prices: the discount is always the real one), ENDS IN 47:59:12 counting down, "Then it's gone for
good." (the pack goes, not just its price), BUY NOW and NOT NOW.

It opens by itself on the title once nothing else is going on (UIRoot._starter_auto): the first time
(the server's clock starts then: Session.starter_seen) and once a session after that while the
offer runs; the title's starter button (StarterButton) opens it any time. NOT NOW or a press outside
the window closes it. BUY NOW opens Roblox's prompt; the server's receipt unlocks the items (server/Purchases),
the inventory says so and the window closes with the unlock sound.

Built at DESIGN logical px and scaled to fit (a UIScale), the same layout on phones and desktop.
Signals: closed.

src/client/UI/Takeover.luau.header:
Solo: take over the nation that eliminated you, for 25 Robux (2026-09-28). Offered on the
ELIMINATED screen and the spectating pill while the nation that conquered you is still alive.
A press pauses the match, then spends a saved credit or opens Roblox's purchase prompt; the server
stores the purchase as a credit (server/Purchases), spends it, and the player takes over
(Session.take_over: its land, army, gold and buildings, its AI off). A purchase whose moment passed
stays saved for the next time a nation conquers the player.

UIRoot drives it: tick() once a second, on_credits() / on_result() from the session, refresh()
when the ELIMINATED screen opens; pending() pauses the solo match.

src/client/UI/TargetCard.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/target_card.gd (UITargetCard)
Touch "look before you act" card: the first tap on a foreign nation (or a coast reached by boat)
selects it and shows who it is, with a big primary order button ("Attack · 12.3K"). A second
tap on the same target, or the button, fires; Ally proposes an alliance; ✕ or a tap elsewhere
closes it. For an ally (kind "ally") it offers Donate and Break alliance, which first asks for
confirmation and spells out the Traitor penalty.

src/client/UI/Telemetry.luau.header:
Match milestones for the Creator Dashboard (src/server/Analytics.luau logs them with Roblox's
AnalyticsService). Solo matches run on this client, so the client reports for every match it plays:
started (mode, map), spawned, first attack, whole minutes alive, eliminated (by whom), the end (won
or lost, rank) or leaving early; plus the title screen, How to Play and Spectate. Sent through
Session.report (OP.ANALYTICS); the server validates and dedupes. Nothing here affects the game.
Every STATE_EVERY_S (and right before leaving) a snapshot: what is happening to the player, where
they stand on land, and the frame rate. The server keeps the latest and logs it when the match ends
with the player quitting or leaving (why do players close the game ~2 minutes in? 2026-09-28).

Once a match, the first SLOW_WINDOW_S in a row under SLOW_FPS is reported with what the frame was
made of ("slow": Telemetry.slow_cause). A player's report, 2026-10-09: down to about 3 fps
near the end of a match, on a desktop, and nothing here could say on what: a MIRV's
warheads did that (Map/TrailBudget) and the player had seen none.

UIRoot drives it: bind(state) on every state change, tick() once a second, title_shown(),
help(where), spectate(); UICtx.send passes every intent to on_intent(intent).

src/client/UI/TitleScreen.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/title_screen.gd (UITitleScreen)
Title screen over the live attract-mode globe: AIRFRONT wordmark, Play Solo with difficulty
chips, Multiplayer with live server status, How to Play, credits. Also shows the "joining
multiplayer" queue card while a match is being prepared.

Also defines GradientText (the wordmark / game-over headline): per-glyph Rubik Heavy with letter
spacing, the WORD_SHADER vertical gradient, the diagonal shine sweep and the fat drop shadow.
Roblox caps TextSize at 100, so glyphs render at a smaller TextSize under a UIScale.

src/client/UI/Tooltip.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/tooltip.gd (UITooltip)
Small glass info card. Three placements: following the cursor (tile hover), anchored above a
control (button hints) or pinned in a corner (tap-to-inspect on touch screens).

Spec table: {title, title_color, swatch (Color3), badge, badge_color, sub, rows: {{k, v, color}},
body, hint, hint_color, hint_icon, footer}

src/client/UI/TopStatus.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/top_status.gd (UITopStatus)
Top-centre status pill: match clock (and time limit), phase, and world-control progress
towards the 80 % victory share for you and the current leader. Phones get a one-line mini pill
(clock · rank · share, a tiny Protected chip) whose tap opens the leaderboard.

Signals: tapped(). Members: panel, rank_provider (() -> number, set by UIRoot).
Methods: apply_layout(), bottom_edge(), on_phase(phase, ticks_left), on_bind(), refresh(),
grace_left(); per frame update(dt).

src/client/UI/TouchRouter.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/touch_router.gd (UITouchRouter)
Multi-touch for the HUD. In Godot only the first finger drove the (mouse-based) ratio slider, so
this node routed any other finger that lands on the slider to it. Roblox GUI objects receive
every finger's InputBegan / InputChanged, so a slider that handles Touch itself needs no routing:
the router then only watches (and never double-drives it). It routes fingers only to a slider
that declares `handles_touch = false` and exposes drag_to_global(logical_pos).

Nothing is consumed here: WorldView tracks every finger too (a HUD finger can still become part
of a pinch); a finger WorldView:touch_owned_by_world(index) claims stops driving the slider.

src/client/UI/TrayFit.luau.header:
Widths in the build row (CommandBar): its slots, and the gold SHOP button that closes it (ShopSlot),
a little wider than a slot while there is anything left to get. The row must stay one row wherever
it can (2026-10-04: the build menu was too big; only the SHOP button shows, so it all stays on
one row), so on a phone the slots narrow first, then the SHOP button narrows to one slot's width,
and only then does the tray take a second row.

Numbers only (no widgets): tests/tray_fit.luau.

src/client/UI/Tutorial.luau.header:
A new player's first match, step by step (Data/Tutorial: the steps and why; 2026-10-04: a new
tutorial for new players, made for phones first). One small goal at a time:
  * a card at the top of the screen: "2 / 6", one short line, a bar for a goal with progress, and
    Skip. Short enough to read at a glance on a phone; it never covers the map's middle or the
    command bar;
  * a tap mark where to tap (two rings closing on a dot, with "Tap here" under it): the map spot or
    the control the step is about. It hides while the player is busy and comes back after
    Data/Tutorial.NUDGE_S without an order;
  * a finished step turns the card green for a moment, with a sound, then the next one comes.
The spawn step has no card (the spawn banner is up there): only the mark on a roomy spot, which
is taken for the player after AUTO_SPAWN_S. The City step tops the player's gold up to a City's
price. A step nobody finishes in STEP_MAX_S is passed over. While it runs the coach's tips are
off (UIRoot); they take over afterwards. While it runs the Attack bar starts at its default and
stops at Data.RATIO_CAP, and an order leaves Data.TROOP_FLOOR of the army's cap at home (UICtx
.ratio_max / .troop_floor): a new player can't empty their nation.

  Tutorial.new(ctx, ui)
  :begin()                 the tutorial match was asked for
  :stop(how)               "done" | "skipped" | "left"
  .active, .finished (Signal: how), .step_done (Signal: funnel step, name), .closed (Signal: the
  last card is gone)

src/client/UI/UIAdvisor.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/ui_advisor.gd
Reactions to the match for the HUD: sounds and toasts for game events that involve you, threat
warnings (a neighbour massing 5x your army, being attacked), first-match coach-mark triggers and
filtering of Sim messages that the UI already presents in a richer form.

src/client/UI/UICtx.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/ui_ctx.gd
Shared context for every UI component: duck-typed handles to Session / WorldView / AudioDirector
(so lightweight stand-ins work in tests), the bound GameState, layout metrics, the attack ratio,
persisted settings and throttled sound effects. Also a few static helpers the Godot builtins
provided (Rect2 maths on Roblox `Rect`, colour conversion, shared-module resolution).

Coordinates: the UI works in LOGICAL px (Godot px of the 1600x900 design; the kit's Widgets.Root
applies one UI scale, see build/notes/ui-kit.md). WorldView / UserInputService use VIEWPORT px.
Every conversion happens here: tile_screen_pos / mouse_pos return logical px, tile_at(pos) takes
logical px, to_view / to_logical convert explicitly.

src/client/UI/UIInteract.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/ui_interact.gd
Globe interaction for the HUD: hover tooltips and previews, primary clicks (spawn / expand /
attack / boat / inspect), build & nuke placement mode, the radial context menu and its actions,
and the keyboard / wheel / touch detection (hotkeys: H, L, Esc, Space, Backspace, Q/E, 1-0;
M / Home live in Main).

Input: UserInputService events, respecting gameProcessedEvent (chat typing never triggers a
hotkey). Positions are viewport coordinates (see UICtx).

src/client/UI/UIKern.luau.header:
GENERATED by tools/uikit/make_kern.py from Rubik's GPOS 'kern' pairs. Do not edit.
Pair kerning in em/1000 per weight for letter-spaced (per-glyph) text: 6-char records
"<first><second><signed value>", e.g. "LT-102" (printable ASCII, |kern| >= 8).

src/client/UI/UILayoutProbe.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/ui_layout_probe.gd (UILayoutProbe)
Layout helpers for UIRoot: measures the platform's own HUD (the Roblox top bar row with Main's
top-bar buttons, the chat window) so our panels stay clear of it, reads the device safe area,
tells the globe which part of the screen is HUD-free, and enforces the 12 px text minimum on
touch screens.

Airship -> Roblox: Airship's top bar = the Roblox top bar row (GuiService.TopbarInset: Roblox's
own buttons sit left of TopbarInset.Min.X, Main's buttons start there); the Airship chat panel
= the TextChatService chat window (ChatWindowConfiguration.AbsolutePosition / AbsoluteSize).

src/client/UI/UIMaps.luau.header:
The playable maps for the UI: the replicated registry (Data/MapList)
joined with the uploaded thumbnails (Assets/MapThumbs, keyed by the source map folder name). Falls
back to the one built-in map when the registry is missing.

src/client/UI/UIRoot.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/ui_root.gd (UIRoot)
AIRFRONT interface root. Built entirely in code: title screen, spawn banner, HUD (command bar,
world-control status, leaderboard, event feed, nuke alert), tooltips, radial menu, help, game
menu and the victory / defeat screen. Wire with setup(session, world, audio) (DESIGN.md §10).

Roblox: one ScreenGui "AirfrontUI" (DisplayOrder 10, above the map-label layer at 0; below
Main's top bar at 50) holding a Widgets.Root (the kit's Godot-like node tree, logical px with
one UI scale). One render-step loop (after the camera) runs every per-frame update, then the
kit's tweens / layout (Widgets.step). Main owns M / Home and the top-bar buttons.

src/client/UI/UIRules.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/ui_rules.gd
Client-side game knowledge for the interface: build/nuke catalogue, costs (via Rules), what a
click on a tile would do, radial-menu contents and placement checks. These are hints only; the
Sim validates every intent for real.
(The GDScript's unused private helpers _site_ok / _nearest_own / _neighbours4 are left out.)

src/client/UI/UITheme.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/ui_theme.gd
AIRFRONT design system: colour tokens, the 8 px spacing scale, Rubik weights, text metrics, the
icon cache, style factories and widget helpers. Everything is static so any component can use it.

Roblox notes (see build/notes/ui-kit.md):
  * Colours: tokens are Color3; a translucent colour is an RGBA {color: Color3, alpha: number}
    made with UITheme.c(col, a) (= Godot `Color(col, a)`) or UITheme.rgba(r, g, b, a). Every kit
    function accepts Color3 or RGBA (or a Core RGBA8 int).
  * Sizes are Godot logical px. The kit renders them at `UITheme.scale` (set by Widgets.Root).
  * Godot font size S (em px) -> Roblox TextSize round(S * 1.185 * scale): Roblox TextSize is the
    line height (ascent + descent), Rubik's is 1.185 em (verified: TextBounds == TTF advances).
  * Text is measured synchronously with a hidden TextLabel once the Rubik weights are loaded
    (UITheme.init() yields until they are); Lune falls back to approximate metrics.

src/client/UI/UnitCard.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/unit_card.gd (UIUnitCard)
Selected-warship card (compact on phones): health bar, veterancy chevrons with kills toward the
next rank, state (Patrolling / Returning to port for repairs / Repairing) and, for your own
ship, the hint "Tap the sea to move". Enemy warships show owner, health and veterancy only.
Reads GameState unit fields defensively (hp, max_hp, veterancy, vet_progress, state).

src/client/UI/Widgets.luau.header:
Port of scripts/ui/widgets.gd (UIWidgets animation helpers) plus the kit's Control engine.

The original UI is built from Godot Controls and Containers. Roblox auto-layout cannot express
them exactly (expand / shrink flags, minimum sizes, fixed-width tabular numbers, letter
spacing, synchronous size queries), so this module implements a small Control tree with Godot
semantics that renders to Roblox GuiObjects:

  Control   free children placed by anchors / offsets / grow direction (Godot Control)
  Box       HBoxContainer / VBoxContainer (separation, alignment, size flags, stretch)
  Panel     PanelContainer with a "panel" style (StyleBoxFlat); Margin = MarginContainer
  Label     Rubik text (alignment, clip / ellipsis, autowrap, letter spacing, tabular digits)
  Icon      TextureRect (UiIcons glyph, tint);  ColorRect
  Button    Button with theme variations (UITheme.theme()), icon + text, toggle mode
  Root      top-level node bound to a ScreenGui / Frame; owns the UI scale & logical viewport

Every node has `node.gui` (its Roblox GuiObject). Sizes and positions are logical px (Godot px);
the engine renders them at UITheme.scale, pixel-snapped. Layout is recomputed for dirty trees
once per frame (Widgets.step) and synchronously whenever a size is queried.
Tweens follow Godot's Tween API and easing equations exactly (create_tween, tween_property,
set_trans / set_ease, set_parallel, chain, tween_interval, tween_callback, tween_method).

src/client/Audio/AudioDirector.luau.header:
Port of scripts/audio/audio_director.gd: music + sound-effect director (client only).

- The soundtrack (Assets/Soundtrack.luau: Rodrigo Flores' Orchestral Ambients, 2026-09-27) plays by
  mood (set_music_mood: title, wait, calm, war, victory, defeat — UIRoot picks it with MusicMood):
  whole tracks, intro to ending, the next one (Playlist: shuffled, no recent repeats) fading in over
  the last TRACK_OVERLAP_S; a new mood crossfades at once, except war -> calm, which lets the battle
  track play out. Only the next track is preloaded (phones). Two music Sounds crossfade
  (equal-power). Without the soundtrack the old looping "menu" / "war" themes play (play_theme).
- Music on/off is persisted per account through the Session's settings ([audio] music_enabled, as
  the original's user://settings.cfg) and fades smoothly (0.6 s); switched-off music is paused so it
  resumes where it was.
- play_sfx() plays from per-effect voice pools (MAX_SAME Sounds per effect, created once with their
  SoundId so every play is already loaded — swapping SoundId per play made Sound.Played fire with
  IsLoaded = false, review P2-7), at most VOICE_COUNT ringing at once, with per-sound throttling,
  a cap on simultaneous copies and voice-steal priorities; long stings honour cooldowns (a repeat
  plays a short accent instead).
- duck_music() dips the music under big moments (nuke explosions etc. duck automatically).
- "Music" and "SFX" SoundGroups under SoundService. Levels are the original's dB values converted
  with Sound.Volume = 10^(dB/20) (Volume is linear gain, 1 = unity; the assets keep the WAVs' levels).
- Sound ids come from Assets/Audio.luau (assets agent); missing entries are skipped silently.
  Assets/AudioExtra (the studio's other games) and then Assets/AudioUI (the interface kit, from
  the same packs: tools/assets/upload_sfx_ui.py) replace same-named entries; a replaced sound stays as that
  name's stand-in, played while the new one has not loaded (still in moderation, or refused).
- pop() is the sound of your border growing (added 2026-10-04, so taking land is heard as well as
  seen): a run of one bubble pop whose rate follows how fast land is being taken, a little
  higher the longer the run lasts.

src/client/Audio/MusicMood.luau.header:
Which soundtrack mood fits the moment (AudioDirector.set_music_mood). Pure logic, polled by UIRoot:
  title    the title screen                     wait     a public match's waiting room
  calm     a match, no fighting                 war      fighting a nation or a player
  victory  the match is over and we won          defeat   the match is over for us (lost, or out)
War: an attack between us and a nation or a player (tribes don't count — early expansion isn't a
war) or a nuke of ours or at our land; it lasts WAR_HOLD_S after the last sign of fighting, so the
music doesn't flip back and forth.

src/client/Audio/Playlist.luau.header:
The soundtrack's playlists (Assets/Soundtrack.luau): which track plays next in a mood. Pure logic
(no Roblox services), used by AudioDirector.

  Playlist.new(manifest, rand?)       manifest = {tracks = {key = {id, length, ...}}, moods = {mood = {keys}}}
  :pool(mood)                         the mood's playable track keys (FALLBACK moods when empty)
  :next(mood)                         the next key: the title's opener first, then shuffled — never one
                                      of the last few played (HISTORY, at most half the pool)
  :after(mood)                        the mood that follows once a track of `mood` ended (victory and
                                      defeat play once)

src/client/Map/AtlasReady.luau.header:
Tells a map layer when an image it would like to switch to can be drawn.

A layer that swaps two stacked images for one combined atlas (Sprites.units_one, Sprites.shapes_one) must not
do so before that atlas loads for this player: an image Roblox has not approved yet, or refuses,
draws nothing, and every unit or plate on the map would be gone. So the layer starts on the atlases
it has always used and asks here.

ContentProvider:PreloadAsync answers truthfully only for an instance: given the content id as a
string it reported Failure for atlases that were on screen (Studio, 2026-10-08), and Success /
Failure correctly for an ImageLabel holding it.

src/client/Map/FalloutGlow.luau.header:
The glow of fresh fallout on the 2D map (2026-10-12, so irradiated land looks better and
glows: the fallout used to be a flat green, with no glow).
How it is made:
  * heat: a tile that turns to fallout is at heat 1, which drains by HEAT_DECAY_PER_TICK / 255 a game
    tick (gone in 25.5 s); a tile no longer fallout is at 0. Fallout already
    on the map when the state is bound has none.
  * the glow is worked out for one tile in every SCALE x SCALE block (its centre tile):
    a "broil" of two value noises, contrast and intensity mixed from
    cold to hot by the heat, a slower meta noise over it, all faded in by the heat; and, on some
    blocks (a hash over the threshold), a dot of light flickering at a rate of its own
    (the extract function). Kept in 0..1 (RGBA8).
  * a 5-tap Gaussian blur across and down (BLUR), then laid over the map, linearly
    filtered, times COVERAGE: one EditableImage
    of the blocks (straight alpha) stretched over the map in one ImageLabel, under the overlays.
Worked out on the CPU, so redrawn UPDATE_S apart, not every frame, its noise (the costly part)
for as many blocks as NOISE_BUDGET_S allows each time, round robin (the noise moves over seconds);
not written on a frame the map surface wrote one of its images (MapSurface: Roblox shows one
EditableImage update a frame), unless it has waited SKIP_MAX frames. (2026-10-26, phones' slow
frames: its lists, noise and buffers are kept from one draw to the next, and the label is placed
again only when the camera moved.)
(2026-10-27, "Script - Fallout Glow" led phones' slow frames: a MIRV's or a few far-apart nukes'
box is most of the image, and it was blurred whole every draw (a MIRV: ~32 ms a draw on a Mac,
interpreted). Now only what the view can reach is drawn (`_win`: the view's blocks and a quarter
view more each way, drawn again at once when the view leaves it for glow not drawn), the blur goes
over the rows with glow and the columns it reaches, sliding along them (one read a cell, not five),
a block's hashes are worked out once, phones redraw at UPDATE_S_MOBILE and a long draw waits DUTY
times as long. The pixels drawn are the same.)

src/client/Map/FrameClock.luau.header:
The client's frame time: the real one (os.clock, RenderStepped's dt), except while a Studio film
(Dev/Film: the trailer, 2026-10-12) steps time itself,
a frame at a time, so a capture of each frame plays back smoothly. The session, the map and the HUD
take their dt from here and the map's animations their clock.

src/client/Map/FrontLayer.luau.header:
Troop counts on the local player's fronts (a label per attack front, floating over the map):
every 200 ms, for each attack by the local player on another owner (blue
#3fa9f5) and each attack on the local player by a player or nation, not a tribe (red #f87171),
the front is split into connected clusters (8-neighbours); the two largest (clusters under 30
full-size tiles dropped, the largest always kept) get a label with the attack's troops
(render_troops) at the front tile nearest the cluster's centroid. Labels glide to new positions
over 250 ms (snap beyond 200 full-size tiles) and keep a constant on-screen size.

The front: the label belongs on the attack's frontier, the whole shared border; the
client has no frontier, so it uses the local player's border tiles (UI BorderTracker, handed
over with set_borders) that touch the other owner.
(2026-10-26, phones' slow frames: a poll works in tables kept from one poll to the next, and a label
is written only what changed.)

src/client/Map/FxLayer.luau.header:
Effects on the 2D map: a nuke's shockwave ring grows to 1.5 x its
blast radius over 1.5 s behind a white flash, a destroyed ship / shot-down nuke pops a small
ring (0.8 s), and the camera shakes a little for nukes near the view. Pooled GUI circles.
Conquests by the local player (a flag and a gold popup): a victory
flag planted at the conquered name's location, its banner the conqueror's colour (Assets/MapFx:
10 frames of 24 x 24 at 90 ms, drawn 22 full-size tiles wide, 2.5 s, fade in over the first 10 % and
out after 60 %; 2026-10-25: it replaced a sword clash for the elimination), and a
white "+ 12.3K" gold line below it (font 6 tiles, fading
linearly).
Both keep a minimum on-screen size, so a zoomed-out map still shows them.
Income (2026-10-07:
trains show the little money-increase popup as they pass through cities too): gold the local
player earned at a tile, a train's stop at a station, is a white "+ 25.0K" that starts 3 full-size tiles
above the tile, rises 3 tiles a second and fades out over 1.5 s (font 6 tiles). It keeps a minimum
size on screen and is not drawn on a map zoomed far out (and is never bigger than
40 px).
Explosions (Assets/MapFx; added 2026-10-04 for a destroyed defense post and for a
nuke shot down by a SAM): a
destroyed defense post or Arsenal structure plays `building` over a small ring, a nuke shot
down plays `sam` where it was. They are seen, not heard (shots and hits were made silent
on 2026-09-27: together they were a constant racket).
Nukes (since
2026-10-12; the trailer's hydrogen bombs fell flat when a ring and a green stain were all
a nuke left): a nuke that lands plays the explosion (Assets/MapFx: 12 frames of
60 x 60 at 70 ms, drawn 60 full-size tiles wide) and leaves debris burning: mini fires, smoke, big
smoke and smoke with fire (DEBRIS_PLAN, looping) scattered within half its radius, 6 s, fading in
over the first 10 % and out after 80 %; its ring grows to 1.5 x that radius. The radius is the
look's (NUKE_FX_RADIUS), not the blast's.
Every pooled object remembers what it was last given and is written only what changed (2026-10-26,
phones' slow frames: a nuke's 240 debris sprites were written six properties each a frame, with the
view still and between their frames), and spent effects leave their lists in one pass, in order.

src/client/Map/MapCamera.luau.header:
2D map camera for a flat tile map drawn in the GUI.

Map space: u = tile column + fraction (0..W), v = tile row + fraction (0 = top edge .. H); a
tile's centre is (x + 0.5, y + 0.5). Maps are flat rectangles (nothing wraps).
Screen space: viewport px (Camera.ViewportSize / InputObject.Position + GuiInset).

The view is (cu, cv, scale): the map point (cu, cv) sits at the view anchor — the viewport centre
moved by screen_offset (the middle of the HUD-free area, MapView.set_safe_area) — and one tile is
`scale` px wide. Once the map is bigger than the view it pans until an edge reaches the view
anchor; smaller, it stays centred (clamp_axis).

It also provides the camera-rig API the input controller uses (halt, viewport_size, pan,
zoom_by, globe_hit, is_moving, begin_drag, drag_by, end_drag), so the input keeps GlobeInput's
touch / mouse model.
(Lune tests load this file with the shared modules from the repo.)

src/client/Map/MapInput.luau.header:
Map input (from scripts/view/globe_input.gd): mouse, trackpad and multi-touch for MapView,
driving the MapCamera through its camera-rig API (drag pans the map, wheel / pinch zoom about
the pointer). "Globe" below means the map.

Touch model (Roblox): every touch is tracked by its InputObject from UserInputService. A touch
whose press was not processed by the GUI (gameProcessedEvent false: no Active GuiObject took it)
landed on free globe (GLOBE); one the GUI processed landed on a HUD control (UI). The GUI keeps
UI touches (taps, slider drags) unless they become part of a pinch.
 * One GLOBE finger: orbit with inertia once it moves past the slop; a drag that crosses a HUD
   panel keeps orbiting. Tap = tile_clicked, still 500 ms press = tile_context.
 * A second finger stops any orbit / inertia at once and cancels the first finger's tap. If both
   fingers are GLOBE the pinch starts immediately; if one started on the HUD it becomes a pinch
   only when BOTH fingers move (a resting thumb on the globe + a tap / slider drag on the HUD
   stays a HUD action). While pinching the globe only zooms (around the point under the
   fingers' start midpoint); no rotation.
 * Lifting fingers after a two-finger gesture never taps; a remaining GLOBE finger may orbit.
 * touch_owned_by_world(io) tells the UI whether the view owns a touch (GLOBE gesture or pinch
   participant); valid through the frame in which the finger lifts, so a HUD control can ignore
   the release of a finger that took part in a pinch.
 * Stale touches (review_code.md R2-6): a finger whose InputEnded never arrives (app backgrounded,
   a system gesture stole it) must not lock the globe. A tracked touch is dropped when its
   InputObject reports End / Cancel, when it has not moved for STALE_TOUCH_S and a new finger
   would otherwise be refused (two tracked already: Roblox sends nothing for a finger held still,
   so age alone never evicts a resting first finger — "rest a thumb, then pinch" stays a pinch),
   when the window loses focus or the Roblox menu opens, and on input on / off.
Stop gesture: pressing (touch or mouse) while the globe is still moving (inertia above
STOP_PX_PER_S or a focus animation) halts it and that press never taps (it may still turn into a
drag, or be held for the menu: holding after a fling used to do nothing, which made the hold
menu seem inconsistent, 2026-09-29). Every press kills inertia.
hold_state() reports a touch hold in progress (UIRoot draws the hold ring from it).
Mouse: left-drag orbit, right-click context, wheel / trackpad pinch / two-finger pan zoom toward
the pointer. WASD / arrows pan and + / - zoom while input_enabled and no TextBox has focus.
All positions are VIEWPORT px (InputObject.Position + GuiService:GetGuiInset()).

src/client/Map/MapSurface.luau.header:
The 2D map surface (terrain, territory and borders): one pixel per
tile, nearest-neighbour upscaled (ResampleMode Pixelated) so tiles stay crisp squares at any zoom.

Terrain and territory are composited on the CPU into one RGBA image of the map, split into
image tiles of at most 1024 x 1024 (the client EditableImage limit), each shown by one ImageLabel
that MapView moves every frame. Only one displayed EditableImage updates per frame (Roblox), so
dirty rows are uploaded round-robin: one image tile per frame, all of its dirty 32-row bands.
  terrain    terrain_pixel of the map's terrain bytes
             (map.tile_bytes: bit7 land, bit6 shoreline, bits0-4 magnitude), colours from
             OCEAN .. MOUNTAIN (e.g. highland #DCCB9E);
  territory  owned tiles blend the owner's colour at 150/255 (saturation 0.85) over the terrain,
             border tiles are opaque in the border colour (HSL lightness - 0.125), fallout ground is
             opaque green noise.
The rules:
  * border tile = a 4-neighbour has another owner (off the map counts as another owner);
  * hovered owner: fill contrast x1.25 about mid-grey, border mixed 25% to white, border thickened
    by one tile (Chebyshev 1). The fill only for an owner of HOVER_FILL_MAX tiles or fewer: it
    means repainting every tile (see HOVER_FILL_MAX);
  * a border next to an ally is mixed 35% toward green;
  * defended tiles (near a same-owner defense post): border checkerboard x0.7, fill x0.85.
(Lune tests load this file with the shared modules from the repo.)

src/client/Map/MapView.luau.header:
The 2D world view (a flat tile map), replacing the 3D globe WorldView with the same
public API (DESIGN.md §10), so UIRoot / Main / Session drive it unchanged:
  signals tile_hovered(tile), tile_clicked(tile), tile_context(tile, screen_pos),
  territory_status_changed(status); bind_state, set_attract_mode, focus_tile, focus_owner,
  set_hover_owner, set_selected_owner, set_selected_unit, unit_at_screen, set_aim,
  aim_sams, set_range_*, set_safe_area, set_hud_rects / controls, local_label_rect,
  set_labels_visible, tile_at_screen, screen_pos_of_tile, camera_distance, project, update.

Rendering: three ScreenGuis under the HUD (DisplayOrder MAP_DISPLAY_ORDER and the two above it):
  RofrontMap        Surface (MapSurface: terrain + territory images, pixel-crisp, wrapped
                    east-west) and the Overlay with what seldom changes: spawn / aim markers,
                    rails, ranges, structure plates;
  RofrontMapUnits   what moves every frame: ships, trains, wakes, munitions, effects, and the
                    structures' progress bars;
  RofrontMapLabels  names and front numbers (they change with the troop counts).
Why three (2026-10-08; players on Windows had stutter bad enough to quit, ten minutes into a
match): Roblox lays out and draws a ScreenGui again as a whole
when anything in it changed, and nothing at all when nothing did. As one ScreenGui the map was
about 13,000 objects twenty minutes into a World match, all of them gone over every frame
because some ship had moved a pixel: 9 ms a frame on the Mac that measured it (with the match
paused: 0.2 ms). The moving layers are a small tree of their own now (docs/performance.md).
Input: MapInput (mouse / touch / keys) driving the MapCamera through the camera-rig API.

src/client/Map/NameLayer.luau.header:
Owner names + troop counts on the 2D map:
  * placement (_place): the bounding box of the owner's main
    cluster, a grid at a coarse scaling factor (1..32 by the box size) where a cell is usable if
    it is the owner's tile, a shoreline tile, ocean with magnitude < 10 or fallout; the largest
    inscribed rectangle of that grid; the name sits at its centre, raised by fontSize / 3, with
    fontSize = min(rect.width / name length * 2, rect.height / 3). Recomputed every 30 ticks
    (REPLACE_TICKS) and at once for new owners; spawn-phase names use an 8-tile box on the spawn;
  * sizing: baseSize = max(1, floor(size)), nameSize = max(4, floor(baseSize *
    0.4)), nameScale = min(baseSize * 0.25, 3); the name line is nameSize * nameScale full-size
    tiles tall, the troop line 0.6 of it; names shorter on screen than the cull threshold hide
    (hovered ones never do). Positions / sizes glide to new targets (LERP_SPEED 10);
  * style: fill black for humans, 0.3 grey nations, 0.4 grey tribes
    (SHADE_*); outline in the owner's colour, width 1.4.
Sizes are in full-size tiles; our tiles are map.k_lin full-size tiles wide.
Roblox: one pooled Frame per owner (name + troops TextLabels with UIStroke); TextSize caps at
100 px, beyond that a UIScale enlarges the whole plate.

src/client/Map/RangeLayer.luau.header:
Range rings on the 2D map: SAM interception coverage and defense-post protection radius, the
prospective ring while placing one, and the selected warship's patrol / targeting rings. The
choice of rings is the globe RangeLayer's (View/RangeLayer.luau _rebuild), drawn as flat GUI
circles (UIStroke keeps widths pixel-constant) with a faint fill:
  mode "auto" (default): own SAMs / posts faint, fading out as the view pulls back; while aiming
  a nuke the hostile SAMs within NEAR_AIM x their range of the aim tile (red-tinted) and those
  covering it (hot: thicker, pulsing; aim_sams() counts them); boat aim / "attack_aim": the
  target owner's posts; hovered / focused sites; the build preview ring (+ own rings of that
  kind at full strength). "nuke_aim", "all", "none" as in the globe layer.
(2026-10-26, phones' slow frames: a ring remembers what it was last given and is written only what
changed, where every ring on screen was written eight properties a frame; the rings are chosen
again only when what they show changes: not for a missile fired, and while a SAM's range grows
after an upgrade only that ring's radius follows it, a game tick at a time.)

src/client/Map/RoadLayer.luau.header:
Railroads on the 2D map: every railroad follows its tile path
(GameState.roads: rid -> {a, b, tiles}) and fades in over FADE_RANGE up to zoom MIN_ZOOM.
Zoomed out it is a line a full-size tile wide along the path's centre (THICKNESS 1: the path's straight
runs, pooled GUI bars); zoomed in, a detailed track (from DETAIL_ZOOM): each tile a
3 x 3 grid, two rails along its sides and a tie between them, a turn's tile its own piece (the two
sides it joins, rail_kinds). The track is a tiled image (assets/rails, RailArt)
along each straight stretch and one per turn.
Coloured by the land under them: grey on unclaimed land, a light rail on the
local player's land (dark over light territory) and the owner's border colour elsewhere; runs are
cut every RUN_MAX tiles so the colour follows the borders they cross. Redrawn when the camera or
the network changes, and now and then for the colours.

(2026-10-12: in the trailer's rail shot the train tracks looked poor; they
were bars 0.4 of a tile wide, 2 px at a continent's zoom, and never the track.)
(2026-10-27, "Script - Roads" was phones' second slow-frame cause: a pan moved every rail on the
screen, one Position each, and a rail coming on or going off the screen handed every rail after it
in the pool another run: six writes each. Now the rails sit in a frame placed at the map's origin
(`_pan`), each where it is at this zoom, so a pan writes the frame alone; until the view has moved
PAN_SLACK px no rail is even looked at (the rails that far off the screen are kept). A run or piece
keeps its GUI object while it is drawn.)

src/client/Map/StructureLayer.luau.header:
Structure icons on the 2D map:
  * a plate per structure in its kind's shape (Assets/MapSprites: City squircle, Port disc, Factory
    cog, Defense Post shield, SAM Launcher dome, Missile Silo bullet, Artillery diamond, Airfield
    runway, Railgun hexagon), fill = the owner's territory colour at HSV value x0.65, rim = the
    border colour (the territory colour for the local player) at value x0.1, a white glyph inside;
    under construction: grey fill 198 / rim 127;
  * size: ICON_SIZE * iconScale px, iconScale = DOT_SCALE (0.3, no glyph)
    when zoom <= DOTS_ZOOM, zoom / GROW_ZOOM above GROW_ZOOM, else
    min(1, zoom / SCALE_FACTOR_OUT); per-kind shape scale; zoom = the camera zoom
    (device px per full-size tile; a tile is k_lin full-size tiles, a GUI px DEVICE_RATIO
    device px);
  * level >= 2: the level number above the plate (0.4 plate sizes up);
  * a progress bar, 14 x 3 full-size tiles centred 6 tiles below the structure
    (1-tile black border; fill red < 25 % < orange < 50 % < yellow < 75 % < green): construction
    progress, and a SAM's / silo's missile readiness while missiles reload (Ev.STRUCT_SHOTS).
Roblox: pooled plates, positions rewritten only when the camera or the structure set changed. A
plate is one ImageLabel with the glyph inside it: the shape's rim and fill in one image
(Sprites.shapes_one, tinted with the fill colour: its rim pixels are the grey that makes the rim's
tenth of the value). It was a Frame holding a rim image, a fill image, the glyph and a level
label, five objects for each of a late game's 500 structures, all laid out again on every camera
move (2026-10-08, docs/performance.md). The level label is made when a structure has a level to
show. While shapes_one has not loaded, every plate keeps a second image for the fill.
(2026-10-26, phones' slow frames: a plate and its bar remember what they were last given and are
written only what changed, read nothing back from Roblox; a structure's own event redraws that
structure alone, where every SAM shot on the map used to redraw every plate.)

src/client/Map/TrailBudget.luau.header:
How much of the munitions in flight UnitLayer draws: every trail dot and every target ring is a
GUI object, so their number has a ceiling whatever the Sim has in the air.

A munition's trail is a dot every UnitLayer.TRAIL_STEP along the arc it has flown, MAX at most. All
the munitions in flight share BUDGET dots a redraw: with more of them than the budget feeds whole
trails, each keeps only its newest dots (the tail behind it), down to none.
  * A MIRV is 350 warheads (Rules.MIRV_WARHEADS), and the AI fires them at a leader who nears the
    win. Each warhead had its whole trail and a pulsing target ring. One MIRV on a World map,
    measured 2026-10-09 on the Mac that measures docs/performance.md: 208 warheads, 16,784 objects
    in the unit layer where 1,000 had been, 27 ms of its script a frame where 2 had been, frames of
    183 ms. A player's report the same day: "I went down to like 3fps nearing the end of a rofront
    game".
  * so the trails share a budget, and MIRV warheads lose their target rings while many fly.

Pure Luau (no Roblox types): tests/trail_budget.luau.

src/client/Map/UnitLayer.luau.header:
Units on the 2D map:
  * sprites from the unit atlas (13 x 13 px, drawn 13 full-size tiles wide, so they
    scale with the map), recoloured: light pixels in the owner's territory
    colour, dark pixels in its border colour (two tinted mask layers, Pixelated);
  * ships / trains follow their path tile to tile (the sim's timing: start_tick +
    ticks_per_tile); warships interpolate prev_tile -> current over a second;
  * a train is drawn as the engine, TRAIN_CARRIAGES carriages and a
    tail engine, TRAIN_SPACING full-size tiles apart along the rails behind it (the sim moves one
    unit; the cars are cosmetic);
  * nukes fly a cubic Bezier (Rules.nuke_arc: control points a quarter / three quarters
    along, raised by max(dist / 3, 50 full-size tiles) toward the top, clamped to the map; the
    Sim flies the same arc), leave a trail in the owner's colour (alpha 0.588) and mark their
    target with a pulsing blast ring;
  * shells and SAM missiles are small sprites flying straight to their target;
  * transport ships leave a wake: the way sailed so far,
    one full-size tile wide in the owner's territory colour at alpha 0.588, gone with the ship.
    The ship and its wake follow the route with its corners rounded (Map/WakeRoute: the Sim's
    paths are straight legs meeting at sharp corners, and the wake was a few straight bars until
    2026-10-07, when it was made to curve smoothly), drawn as short straight bars.

What it costs (2026-10-08; players on Windows had stutter bad enough to quit, ten minutes into a
match). Twenty minutes into a World match there are 700 units, and with the
whole map in view this layer was the frame's biggest cost: 2.9 of the map's 3.5 ms of script a frame,
about 3,000 GUI objects and some 9,000 Position writes a second for Roblox to lay out again
(docs/performance.md has the trace). So:
  * a train's cars are drawn only where they can be told apart (CARS_MIN_ZOOM, where the rails fade
    in too): 2 full-size tiles apart, seven 13-tile sprites are one blob on a map zoomed out, yet
    they were six of every seven sprites that moved;
  * a sprite is one image (Sprites.units_one: both of the sprite's colours in one tint) once that atlas
    has loaded, and until then two, the second inside the first; it was two inside a frame;
  * while the camera stands still and many sprites are on screen, the whole layer is redrawn 20 to
    30 times a second, not every frame (THROTTLE_*): at that zoom a ship moves a fraction of a
    pixel a frame, and a frame in which nothing here changes costs Roblox nothing (MapView's
    header);
  * the pools keep a few spares and destroy the rest (POOL_SPARE): every object in this ScreenGui
    is gone over on each frame something moved, shown or not, and the pools had grown to 7,700.

src/client/Map/ViewRules.luau.header:
Port of scripts/view/view_rules.gd — gameplay numbers the view draws (SAM / defense ranges, nuke
radii, interception odds), read from Rules at runtime so range rings and aim previews follow the
Sim when it is retuned. Prefers Rules' functions and falls back to the older constants.

Range metric (must match the Sim): covered <=> (dx * xs)^2 + dy^2 <= r^2 in grid tiles, dx wrapping
at W, xs = max(cos(lat of the target tile's row), 0.08) — Defs.range_d2 == SimState.range_d2.

src/client/Map/WakeRoute.luau.header:
A transport ship's route as a smooth line (UnitLayer draws the ship and its wake along it).

The Sim's water paths are string-pulled (SimNav._smooth): long straight legs that meet at sharp
corners in open water, and near a coast, where no straight line is free, a staircase of two-tile
steps. Drawn as they are, a wake was a few straight bars and some jitter (2026-10-07: boat
trails looked like straight lines; they should curve smoothly). Here:
  1. the path is cut into straight legs that stay within TOL tiles of its tiles (a staircase is
     one leg; measured on 200 World routes, 8 of 10 legs were under 8 tiles before);
  2. every corner is rounded: the route leaves a leg up to CORNER full-size tiles before the corner
     (never more than half the leg) and joins the next one as far after it, along a quadratic
     Bezier whose control point is the corner, cut into short straight pieces (one per ARC_STEP
     of turn).
  * The curve passes inside the corner. Where that would put it on land (a corner at a cape; a
    tile's width of shore is let pass, as a leg may) it is tried at half and at a quarter the
    size, and the corner stays sharp if none fits.
  * Each point carries how many path tiles along the route it is (`ss`), so the ship is placed by
    the Sim's own timing (tiles sailed) and reaches both ends of every curve when it would have
    reached them on the legs.

Pure Luau (no Roblox types): tests/wake_route.luau.

src/shared/Data/Stars.luau.header:
Stars: the currency a match pays, spent in the Arsenal (Data/Arsenal; 2026-10-04: an item is either
earned by playing or bought with Robux). The formula is Pixel Conquest's Money payout
(an average match pays an average seat about 1,000; about 3,300 an hour of play), line by line:

  played     100                              not for a player who left early
  survived   15 a minute alive
  territory  30 x peak land in fair shares    (a share = the map's land / the nations and players)
  conquests  54 a nation or player conquered  (tribes don't count: there are hundreds)
  placed     14 a minute x place score        place score = (1 - (place - 1) / (field - 1))^2;
                                              not for a player who left early
  victory    18 a minute                      the winner

Every line is rounded to 5 (at least 5 when it pays at all). A player who never spawned gets
nothing. A solo match pays a share of this by difficulty (MODE_MULT: it runs on the player's own
device against the AI); 2x Stars (Data/Arsenal) doubles the total.

  Stars.payout(result, mode, double) -> { lines = { { key, amount } }, total }
  Stars.sanitize(report, real_minutes) -> result   a client's solo report, made safe
  Stars.solo_cap(real_minutes)                     the most a solo match of that length may pay
  Stars.Tracker.new(sim)                           follows a running Sim for its humans' results

src/shared/Data/Tutorial.luau.header:
A new player's first match (2026-10-04: an updated tutorial for new players, designed for phones
first, since 90% of the players are on a phone, with its steps drawn from the analytics funnels).
The onboarding funnel of the 28 days before it (202,158 new players):

  Joined 100% -> Title 99% -> Match Started 85% -> Spawned 81% -> First Attack 66%
  -> Survived 3 Min 32% -> Survived 10 Min 24% -> Second Match 21%

  * 14% never start a match: the first match starts by itself, on this device, at once;
  * 5% never pick a start: a spot is pointed out, and taken for them after AUTO_SPAWN_S;
  * 19% spawn and never attack: the first step is the first tap, with the place to tap marked;
  * half of those who attack are gone within 3 minutes, while the AI may not even attack them
    yet (Rules.HUMAN_GRACE_TICKS): they leave with nothing to do. So the first minutes are a list
    of small goals with a reward at the end, on a match with fewer tribes in the way (TRIBES)
    and the gentlest AI (DIFFICULTY).

The match is an ordinary solo match otherwise: it goes on after the last step. client/UI/Tutorial
runs the steps; server/Analytics logs them as the "Tutorial" funnel (FUNNEL); the Stars are paid
once per player (server/Purchases.tutorial_bonus).
